title: DM-Tune: Quantizing Diffusion Models with Mixture-of-Gaussian Guided Noise Tuning
problem: Diffusion models require high computational and memory resources; traditional full-precision execution is inefficient; naive mixed-precision quantization adds runtime overhead from format casting and management complexity.
motivation: Efficient deployment of diffusion models on resource-constrained devices requires aggressive quantization while maintaining image quality and text-to-image alignment.
method: DM-Tune uses a simpler approach to compress models: instead of using different precision levels for different parts (which requires costly switching between formats), it converts everything to a single low-precision format. To maintain image quality despite the lower precision, it adds a tuning step that learns to compensate for what was lost, using a mathematical function based on Gaussian distributions (smooth probability curves) and linear adjustments. The system identifies which layers lose quality most easily, measures the quantization errors throughout the model, and runs this compensation efficiently on GPUs with custom code.
key_novelty: A unified low-precision format with Gaussian-guided noise tuning produces better image quality and alignment than mixed-precision quantization while simplifying execution.
contributions: Unified low-precision quantization with noise-tuning mechanism
Custom low-precision GPU kernels with efficient noise-tuning
Demonstrates mixed-precision-quality results in single FP8 format with improved runtime

metrics.quality: surpasses FP32, FP8, and state-of-the-art mixed-precision

primary_theme: Unified low-precision quantization with noise-tuning for diffusion models
